finding.summary: None of the text-editor plumbing that actually produces the affinity is tested (click, shift+click, drag, shift+Home, shift+arrow)
finding.evidence: The user-visible fix is that a click/drag/caret-move on a wrap boundary tags the selection endpoint with `lineAffinity` (text-editor.ts ~1517 mousedown, ~1770 header/footer drag, ~1792 body drag, ~2772 shift+arrow, ~2805 shift+Home). The only new test, packages/docs/test/view/selection-line-affinity.test.ts, hand-constructs DocPositions and calls `computeSelectionRects` directly — it never goes through TextEditor, so it cannot fail if the editor forgets to attach the affinity, attaches the wrong one (e.g. the shift+Home hardcoded 'forward' at offset 0, or shift+Up/Down using the cursor's stale affinity), or drops it on `setRange`. I grepped packages/docs/test for `lineAffinity` (only the new file and hf-caret-selection.test.ts, which tests computeHFCursorPixel), and for `Home|getVisualLineStart|updateDragSelection|mousedown|mousemove` (only cursor-move-no-relayout.test.ts and image-selection-overlay.test.ts, neither of which touches selection affinity). Result: the entire producer side ships with zero coverage while the rect consumer is well covered.

verdict.reason: The affinity-producing paths in text-editor.ts (mousedown at 1517-1525, drag focus at 1776/1798, shift+arrow at 2772-2780, shift+Home hardcoding 'forward' at 2803-2818) are a real behavior change with no test that drives them. The only new test, packages/docs/test/view/selection-line-affinity.test.ts, hand-builds DocPositions and calls computeSelectionRects directly (line 2 import, cases at 91-158), so it passes whether or not the editor attaches any affinity. I searched wide for a counterexample: `affinity` appears in only three test files repo-wide — the new one, hf-caret-selection.test.ts:52-107 (direct computeHFCursorPixel/computeHFSelectionRects calls, no editor), and packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store-concurrent.integration.ts:441-472, which covers only the caret round-trip through the Yorkie store (its selection-endpoint cases at 474-529 assert endpoints with no lineAffinity and never touch TextEditor). The only docs test using MouseEvent is editor-contextmenu.test.ts:68 (right-click menu); cursor-move-no-relayout.test.ts:115-136 presses ArrowRight/ArrowDown but asserts only measureText call counts with no shift; all shiftKey usages in docs tests are Tab/Cmd+Shift+C/read-only paths; there is no setRange affinity-preservation test (cell-range-expand.test.ts:120-148 is unrelated); and no Playwright/Cypress e2e suite exists. Under the test-adequacy rubric this is a clear behavior change shipped with zero meaningful coverage on the producer side — major and blocking.

finding.summary: lineAffinity round-trip through Yorkie anchoring/presence has no test, in a package with no tsc either
finding.evidence: The diff threads `lineAffinity` through `anchorDocPosition`, `anchorDocRange`, `clampPosToModel`, `resolveAnchoredDocPosition`, `fallbackAnchoredDocPosition` and `updateCursorPos`, and changes `anchorDocPosition`'s default from `'backward'` to `undefined` (affecting `setCompositionStart` and everything that resolves an anchor back). I grepped packages/frontend/tests for `lineAffinity`/`affinity` — no matches — and the existing `resolveAnchoredLocalCursor` tests in packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts (lines ~1836-2026) assert only blockId/offset. So nothing verifies the affinity survives anchor→resolve, nor that dropping it for composition anchors is intentional. packages/frontend has no `tsc --noEmit` lane, so even a type-level slip here is uncaught.

verdict.reason: The claim is that the lineAffinity anchor->resolve round-trip in yorkie-doc-store has no test. A direct counterexample exists in the frontend integration lane: packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store-concurrent.integration.ts:441-472, test 'carries a caret lineAffinity across an upstream edit, and adds none when absent'. It sets a caret with lineAffinity 'forward' via updateCursorPos, applies an upstream insertText from the other client, syncs, and asserts resolveAnchoredLocalCursor().cursor deepEquals { blockId, offset: 9, lineAffinity: 'forward' } — the 5->9 offset shift proves the real anchoring path ran rather than echoing the input. It then re-sets a caret with no affinity and asserts the resolved cursor deepEquals { blockId, offset: 5 }, pinning exactly the 'lineAffinity: undefined is an own property' hazard documented at packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:966-972. Nothing is mocked: packages/frontend/tests/helpers/two-user-docs-yorkie.ts:33 creates two live Yorkie clients against YORKIE_RPC_ADDR. It also executes in CI: .github/workflows/ci.yml:551-590 sets YORKIE_RPC_ADDR and starts a Yorkie container (line 721), step 'Verify Integration Lane' (line 749) runs pnpm verify:integration, which at scripts/verify-integration.mjs:56-58 invokes the frontend test:integration script = tsx --test tests/**/*.integration.ts (packages/frontend/package.json:16). The test carries no skip marker beyond the env gate CI satisfies. The reviewer only grepped .test.ts files under packages/frontend/tests, so the .integration.ts lane was never searched.
